system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: Input context: System prompt, memory, skills, and tool prompts define what the agent starts with.
system_prompt_style.evidence_locator: docs Deep Agents overview, Context management
system_prompt_style.note: System prompt assembled from user prompt, memory AGENTS.md, skill frontmatter, and tool prompts; no source code in the evidence bundle.

env_context_strategy.evidence_locator: docs Deep Agents overview, Virtual filesystem access
env_context_strategy.note: The ls/read_file/glob/grep tools are available. Memory and skill frontmatter are also injected at startup.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: Compression: Built-in offloading and summarization compress conversation history and large intermediate results.
context_compaction.evidence_locator: docs Deep Agents overview, Summarization and context offloading
context_compaction.note: Large tool results are offloaded to disk, coded here as tool_output_pruning.

observation_format.evidence_quote: Also supports returning multimodal content blocks for non-text files (images, video, audio, and documents).
observation_format.evidence_locator: docs Deep Agents overview, Virtual filesystem access
observation_format.note: read_file returns image blocks, so screenshots could arguably apply. No code in the bundle to confirm the conversion.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: works with any LLM that supports tool calling: frontier, open-weight, or local
tool_call_format.note: The bundle contains no parser code. An opt-in QuickJS eval interpreter (code_as_action style) is also documented.

tool_count.evidence_quote: The harness includes a built-in task tool that lets the main agent create ephemeral subagents
tool_count.note: Count = 7 filesystem tools (ls, read_file, write_file, edit_file, delete, glob, grep) + task. write_todos is opt-in since v0.7 and not counted. execute is only present with a sandbox backend. The listed values sum to 8, but 9 was recorded; this needs reconciling by the human verifier. Maximal configuration adds execute, write_todos and eval.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: edit_file Perform exact string replacements in files (with global replace mode)
edit_primitive.evidence_locator: docs Deep Agents overview, Virtual filesystem access
edit_primitive.note: write_file: Create a new file, or overwrite an existing one.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: Pass custom functions, LangChain tools, or tools from any MCP server with the tools= parameter.
tool_schema_source.evidence_locator: docs Deep Agents overview, Tools and MCP
tool_schema_source.note: Schemas for Python functions are derived from their signatures and docstrings via LangChain. This is inferred; no code in the bundle.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: Deep Agents fully support the Model Context Protocol (MCP)
protocol_standardization.evidence_locator: docs Deep Agents overview, Tools and MCP
protocol_standardization.note: other = ACP: libs/acp/deepagents_acp/server.py exists in the file tree, and the docs say 'Use deep agents in code editors with ACP'.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: It is the same core tool calling loop as other agent frameworks
loop_primitives.evidence_locator: docs Deep Agents overview, Core capabilities
loop_primitives.note: event_driven is based on LangGraph typed event streams. The ralph_mode example is not shipped configuration.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: Starting in v0.7 task planning is opt-in only. In earlier versions, task planning middleware was included by default.
planning_granularity.evidence_locator: docs Deep Agents overview, Task planning
planning_granularity.note: Opt-in TodoListMiddleware provides explicit_plan_object (write_todos). Coded implicit per the default, though no prompt recipe was seen.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: Use the default general-purpose subagent (enabled by default) or define custom subagents.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: Fresh context: Each invocation creates a new agent instance with its own context.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: Enable this behavior with the interrupt_on parameter in create_deep_agent.
human_in_loop.note: Off by default. It is enabled per tool via interrupt_on.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: Tasks support status tracking ('pending', 'in_progress', 'completed') and are persisted in agent state.
short_term_state.evidence_locator: docs Deep Agents overview, Task planning
short_term_state.note: LangGraph agent state includes virtual filesystem files beyond messages. Todos are opt-in.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: Memory uses AGENTS.md files that you pass through the memory parameter when creating the agent.
long_term_memory.note: Skills are loaded from SKILL.md directories.

state_persistence.note: Relies on LangGraph checkpointer and durable execution. A checkpointer must be supplied.

self_verification.note: The evidence bundle contains no run-loop or middleware source. value should be null: the empty array is a coding error. The rubric_middleware example is not shipped default.

retry_policy.note: No run-loop code in the bundle.

rollback.note: The tool list has no undo. However, the tool list is not the place rollback would be declared, and the backend code is absent.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: Autonomous execution: The subagent runs independently until completion.
termination_condition.note: The loop ends when the model stops calling tools. LangGraph recursion limit is not shown in the evidence.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: Prompt caching is enabled by default when using an Anthropic model, or a Bedrock model (Claude or Nova). No configuration is required.
cost_controls.evidence_locator: docs Deep Agents overview, Prompt caching
cost_controls.note: The code tree has bundled_prices.json for the CLI. Budgets are not evidenced.

timeouts.note: No backend or config code in the bundle.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: The harness provides a configurable virtual filesystem which can be backed by different pluggable backends: in-memory state, local disk, LangGraph store, composite routing, or a custom backend
execution_isolation.evidence_locator: docs Deep Agents overview, Virtual filesystem access
execution_isolation.note: Default in-process virtual FS with no shell. Sandbox backends (container/remote) are optional.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: The harness provides a configurable virtual filesystem which can be backed by different pluggable backends: in-memory state
filesystem_access.evidence_locator: docs Deep Agents overview, Virtual filesystem access
filesystem_access.note: Declarative permissions= rules can scope access.

network_policy.note: No sandbox/network config in the bundle.

permission_model.evidence_quote: If no rule matches, the operation is allowed.
permission_model.evidence_locator: docs Deep Agents overview, Filesystem permissions
permission_model.note: Default has no rules. Optional permissions= is a static allow/deny list; interrupt_on offers per-call prompts.

tracing.evidence_quote: built on LangGraph (streaming, persistence, checkpointing) with first-class tracing, evaluation, and deployment via LangSmith
tracing.note: The CLI has libs/code/deepagents_code/_tracing.py, but OTel is not evidenced.

eval_hooks.note: Eval workflows ship in the repo (evals.yml, harbor.yml).

guardrails.evidence_quote: Filesystem permissions: declarative access control over which paths agents can read or write
guardrails.evidence_locator: docs Deep Agents overview, Execution environment
guardrails.note: Opt-in. The README says 'trust the LLM' model.

target_domain.evidence_quote: You can use deep agents for any task, including complex, multi-step tasks.
target_domain.note: swe via Deep Agents Code; research via the deep_research example.

open_source.evidence_quote: Deep Agents is an open source agent harness
open_source.note: MIT per badge. LICENSE:1 was not shown.

first_release_date.note: No tag history in the bundle.
